persona.summary: A comparative political scientist whose work sits close to political economy. His research asks why countries become and stay democratic, why some states govern impartially and with little corruption, and how political regimes can be measured at scale and over long periods. On an economics committee he brings the perspective of political institutions, bureaucracy, state capacity and institutional measurement.
persona.research_lens: He treats institutions as both outcomes and causes. He asks how regimes and impartial bureaucracies emerge historically, especially through Swedish and European state-building. He also asks how regimes, participation structures and administrative rules shape political and economic outcomes across countries and over time. All three profiles infer that this makes him attentive to economics work on development, political economy, state capacity, corruption and institutions. G also stresses a distinction between how power is accessed (democratic accountability) and how it is exercised (impartial administration).
persona.methods_and_evidence: His work relies on large-N cross-national panel data, regime typologies and expert-coded indicators with explicit measurement and aggregation models (V-Dem). It also draws on historical-comparative evidence, notably on Swedish state-building. He gives concept validity, measurement reliability and data quality as much weight as identification. O adds attention to robustness across samples and to endogeneity between institutions and development.
persona.what_they_value_in_contributions: Inferred from his record: conceptual clarity and valid, transparent operationalization of abstract institutional concepts such as impartiality, meritocracy, polyarchy and regime type. He likely values evidence that travels across countries and long historical periods, and durable public data or frameworks that enable cumulative research. Interdisciplinary relevance across economics, political science, history and public administration also matters to him.
